title: Unramified schemes over a field are disjoint unions of finite separable spectra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if $X$ is a disjoint union (possibly empty and with an arbitrary index set) of spectra $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, where each $L_i/k$ is a finite separable algebraic field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), parts (1) and proof, lines 7790-7821

proof.text: Assume $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified. Choose an affine open cover $X=\bigcup_a U_a$, with $U_a\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, using the local affineness in the definition of a scheme. Restriction to an open subscheme preserves unramifiedness, so every $U_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified. The affine unramified-algebra decomposition supplies a finite set of fields $L_{a,1},\ldots,L_{a,n_a}$, each finite separable over $k$, and a $k$-algebra isomorphism $C_a\cong\prod_{j=1}^{n_a}L_{a,j}$. The empty product is allowed for empty affine charts.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), proof of (1), affine expansion via Algebra Tag 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime), proof, and Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); restriction Tag 02G6 (lemma-unramified-characterize)

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and choose $a$ with $x\in U_a$. Apply the finite-product-spectrum statement to the decomposition in step 1. Its distinct projection kernels exhaust the primes, so exactly one factor index $j$ corresponds to $x$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L_{a,j}\to\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_jL_{a,j})\cong U_a$ identifies its source with the open subscheme whose underlying set is $\{x\}$. Since $U_a$ is open in $X$, this is also the open subscheme $X_x=X|_{\{x\}}$ of $X$. The identification is over $k$: the composite of the structure map $k\to C_a\cong\prod_jL_{a,j}$ with projection to $L_{a,j}$ is precisely that factor's $k$-algebra structure, and taking spectra reverses these composites. Thus $X_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}L_x$ over $k$ for the finite separable extension $L_x=L_{a,j}$.

source.place: Tags 00ED (lemma-spec-product), 00EC (lemma-idempotent-spec), 00E4 (lemma-standard-open), applied to the affine expansion of Morphisms Tag 02G7(1)

proof.text: The open subschemes $X_x$ from step 2, indexed by the underlying set of points of $X$, are pairwise disjoint and cover $X$. This gives the required disjoint union as schemes, not just as spaces: for every open $V\subseteq X$, the sheaf axiom on the disjoint cover $V=\coprod_{x\in V}\{x\}$ identifies $\mathcal O_X(V)$ with $\prod_{x\in V}\mathcal O_X(\{x\})$, with coordinate restriction maps. These are exactly the sections and restriction maps on the disjoint union of the $X_x$, so its evident bijection to $X$ identifies both the topology and the structure sheaf. All identifications are over $k$ by step 2. If $X$ is empty, use the empty index set; no finiteness of the full point set is required.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), proof of (1), discrete-space/disjoint-union sentence; sheaf axiom spelled out

proof.text: Conversely, let $X\cong\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ over $k$, with every $L_i/k$ finite separable. Each $\operatorname{Spec}L_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale by the finite-separable-extension theorem. By the definition of etale, this morphism is unramified. The affine unramifiedness criterion therefore says that $k\to L_i$ is of finite type and has $\Omega_{L_i/k}=0$.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), finite separable extension paragraph; Morphisms Tags 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), converse, and 02G6 (lemma-unramified-characterize)

proof.text: The summands $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ are affine open subschemes covering $X$, and the target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine. Step 4 supplies on each chart the finite-type ring map with zero differentials required by the affine-cover formulation of unramifiedness in the definition. Consequently $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified. For $I=\varnothing$, the pointwise condition (unramified at every point of $X$) is vacuous, so the same implication includes the empty scheme.
